_status: Web demo for the 'attack-path' slide. The seven links keep the deck slide's wording; each names the MITRE ATT&CK tactic it matches (tactic names come from src/data/attack.json, built by npm run attack). Three defenses are the deck's examples (delivery, exploitation, actions on objectives); the others are the course's controls, not a complete list.
title: Attackers move in steps

links.name: Delivery
links.plain: Send it, such as by phishing

defenses.label: Share less about the office online
Staff spot and report the phishing email
MFA and limited access keep the data out of reach

scenes.title: No defenses: the attack runs to the end
scenes.text: Each step leads to the next. Nothing stops it, so it ends with data stolen and files locked.

scenes.title: Email filtering breaks it at Delivery
scenes.text: The phishing email never reaches Ben. Steps 4 to 7 never happen.

scenes.title: The filter misses one. Staff spot and report it
scenes.text: No filter catches everything. Ben spots the phishing email and reports it: the attack stops at Delivery.

scenes.title: Ben clicks. The weakness was already patched
scenes.text: People make mistakes on a busy payout day. The attack needs an old weakness, but it was patched: it stops at Exploitation.

scenes.title: Everything else failed: MFA and limited access
scenes.text: The attacker gets in and reaches the last step, but MFA and limited access keep the data out of reach.

scenes.title: Each step is a chance to stop them
scenes.text: With every defense on, the chain breaks at the first step it can. Each control you add is one more chance to stop it, early.
